title: British Columbia Societies Act guide pack
description: BC-focused guide tracks for societies, with point-in-time source links for date-sensitive checks. Current registered rules are reviewed snapshots; historical application requires a separately verified effective period. Privacy scope is assessed from operations and activities on the Privacy page.

content.summary: Meetings before Nov 28, 2016 belong to the former Society Act track, not the current Societies Act baseline.
content.tooltip: Use the former Society Act point-in-time archive for this date. Current BC Societies Act quorum, notice, electronic meeting, and proxy checks should not be applied automatically.
content.caveat: This app flags the historical source track only; it does not yet encode every pre-2016 rule.

provenance.changeNote: Inherited guide wording; date records its last review, not statutory commencement.

content.summary: BC bylaws are the local rule source for meeting procedures, including any quorum greater than the statutory default.
content.tooltip: Use this guide to keep society-specific bylaw rules separate from the statutory floor. A bylaw rule version should cite the filed bylaw or amendment that created it.
content.caveat: A society's filed bylaws can be stricter where the Act allows.

provenance.changeNote: Current rule and source metadata reuse the shared legal registry. Review and consolidation dates do not establish commencement.

content.summary: Constitution and bylaw alterations generally require a special resolution and take effect on filing the alteration application.
content.tooltip: Constitution and bylaw alterations generally require a special resolution and take effect on filing the alteration application.
content.caveat: The normal meeting threshold is two-thirds of votes cast; applicable higher bylaw thresholds and special transition provisions must be checked. A written special resolution requires all voting members.

provenance.changeNote: Current rule and source metadata reuse the shared legal registry. Review and consolidation dates do not establish commencement.

content.summary: Hold an AGM each calendar year after the incorporation year. A unanimous written resolution addressing all required annual business can be a deemed AGM.
content.tooltip: Hold an AGM each calendar year after the incorporation year. A unanimous written resolution addressing all required annual business can be a deemed AGM.
content.caveat: There is no general fifteen-month rule in the current Societies Act. An approved postponement under s. 71(3) is attributed to the preceding calendar year; retain the authorization and specified date.

content.summary: Notice timing/content rules changed around electronic meeting amendments before the current 2023 wording.
content.tooltip: For meetings before May 4, 2023, use the BC Laws point-in-time source for the exact notice wording in force on that date.
content.caveat: The app points to the correct historical source track but does not yet encode every notice-delivery variant.

provenance.changeNote: Current rule and source metadata reuse the shared legal registry. Review and consolidation dates do not establish commencement.

content.summary: Send written general-meeting notice to every member 14–60 days before the meeting; bylaws can specify a minimum of at least seven days.
content.tooltip: Send written general-meeting notice to every member 14–60 days before the meeting; bylaws can specify a minimum of at least seven days.
content.caveat: The current s. 77(2) alternative requires more than 100 members, enabling bylaws, email to all recorded email addresses and the prescribed publication or website posting. Required notice content and electronic instructions are in s. 78.

provenance.changeNote: Inherited guide wording; date records its last review, not statutory commencement.

content.summary: Member proposal thresholds are based on voting members, with bylaws able to lower the percentage where allowed.
content.tooltip: Use this as the statutory baseline for AGM member-proposal intake, then apply any lower bylaw threshold stored in the bylaw rule version.
content.caveat: The proposal wording and delivery rules should be checked against the point-in-time source.

provenance.changeNote: Inherited guide wording; date records its last review, not statutory commencement.

content.summary: Voting members can requisition a general meeting using the Act's threshold unless bylaws provide a lower percentage.
content.tooltip: This guide track supports member-requisition workflows and should be paired with the bylaw rule version for the meeting date.
content.caveat: Use the point-in-time source for older requisition wording.

provenance.changeNote: Current rule and source metadata reuse the shared legal registry. Review and consolidation dates do not establish commencement.

content.summary: General-meeting quorum is three voting members, or a greater bylaw quorum. If fewer voting members exist, all of them form quorum.
content.tooltip: General-meeting quorum is three voting members, or a greater bylaw quorum. If fewer voting members exist, all of them form quorum.
content.caveat: An adjourned-meeting exception requires enabling bylaws. Section 67 governs membership; it is not the quorum provision.

content.summary: Before the May 20, 2021 amendments, electronic participation used older communication wording and facilitation obligations differed.
content.tooltip: For meetings before May 20, 2021, use the point-in-time s.83 text rather than the current electronic-meeting rule.
content.caveat: Bylaws may have restricted or shaped electronic participation.

provenance.changeNote: Inherited guide wording; date records its last review, not statutory commencement.

content.summary: Unless bylaws say otherwise, eligible participants may attend by telephone or other communications medium when participation requirements are met.
content.tooltip: Electronic and hybrid meeting checks should cite the rule in force on the meeting date and any bylaw override.
content.caveat: Fully electronic meetings carry separate facilitation and notice-instruction requirements.

provenance.changeNote: Inherited guide wording; date records its last review, not statutory commencement.

content.summary: Voting rights and one-vote rules start in the Act, with class and good-standing limits controlled by bylaws where allowed.
content.tooltip: Use this guide when checking who could vote on resolutions before applying bylaw-specific voting-class rules.
content.caveat: Voting by mail, delegate, or electronic means depends on bylaw authority.

content.summary: Before Oct 28, 2021, the proxy rule used older wording but still depended on bylaw permission.
content.tooltip: For meetings before Oct 28, 2021, use the point-in-time s.85 text and the bylaw rule version effective on the meeting date.
content.caveat: Proxy authority is bylaw-dependent.

provenance.changeNote: Inherited guide wording; date records its last review, not statutory commencement.

content.summary: Proxy voting is not available unless the society's bylaws permit it.
content.tooltip: Store proxy permission in the dated bylaw rule version, then cite this statutory guide for the default BC position.
content.caveat: A valid proxy appointment still has to meet Act and bylaw requirements.

provenance.changeNote: Current rule and source metadata reuse the shared legal registry. Review and consolidation dates do not establish commencement.

content.summary: An ordinary written resolution must be sent to every voting member and receive consent from at least two-thirds of voting members. A written special resolution requires all voting members.
content.tooltip: An ordinary written resolution must be sent to every voting member and receive consent from at least two-thirds of voting members. A written special resolution requires all voting members.
content.caveat: Count eligible voting members, not signatures from arbitrary names or workspace users. A deemed AGM needs unanimity and all required annual business under s. 72.

provenance.changeNote: Current rule and source metadata reuse the shared legal registry. Review and consolidation dates do not establish commencement.

content.summary: Keep formation and registry records, orders, registers, consents, disclosures, minutes, resolutions, financial statements and accounting records. Access depends on the record and requester.
content.tooltip: Keep formation and registry records, orders, registers, consents, disclosures, minutes, resolutions, financial statements and accounting records. Access depends on the record and requester.
content.caveat: The member register contains only names and contact information and is organized by class. Do not publish it. Other operational member information belongs in separate restricted records.

content.summary: The model general-meeting quorum is the greater of three voting members and ten percent; model directors’ quorum is a majority.
content.tooltip: The model general-meeting quorum is the greater of three voting members and ten percent; model directors’ quorum is a majority.
content.caveat: Only an adopted model provision controls the organization. Schedule 1 records its amendment by BC Reg 114/2022. The statutory general quorum is separately in s. 82.

content.summary: The BC Model Bylaws do not permit proxy voting.
content.tooltip: Use this guide only if the society adopted the Model Bylaws or uses equivalent proxy wording.
content.caveat: Other BC bylaws may permit proxies because the Act allows bylaw permission.

content.summary: File within 30 days of the held or deemed AGM. If none was held when required, report that fact by January 31 of the next year.
content.tooltip: File within 30 days of the held or deemed AGM. If none was held when required, report that fact by January 31 of the next year.
content.caveat: If an authorized extended AGM deadline is missed, s. 73(3) requires the no-AGM report within 30 days after that deadline. Filing a no-AGM report does not cure the missed meeting.

content.summary: Member inspection under the Act is free. Public access requires bylaw permission and excludes the member register; copies have separate rights and fees.
content.tooltip: Member inspection under the Act is free. Public access requires bylaw permission and excludes the member register; copies have separate rights and fees.
content.caveat: Directors inspect and obtain copies free. One copy of current governing documents and latest financial statements is free to a member. Requested copies are due promptly and no later than 14 days after request and applicable payment. Regulation ss. 4–7 cap fees.

content.summary: Records may cease to be required only after ten years from creation or last alteration and only when no longer relevant.
content.tooltip: Records may cease to be required only after ten years from creation or last alteration and only when no longer relevant.
content.caveat: This is not automatic deletion permission; consider tax rules, litigation holds, ongoing relevance, and other retention duties. Electronic records must be accessible and reproducible.
